```{webr}
#| label: load opt data for table 1
#| envir: table_1
#| echo: false
#| autorun: true
opt_data <- readRDS("data/opt_data.rds") |> 
  dplyr::select(
    c("PID", "Group", 
      "Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education",
      "Prev.preg","Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab",
      "previous_live_preterm_birth",
      "Spont.ab", "Induced.ab", "Any.stillbirth",
      "Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab", 
      "Diabetes", "Hypertension", "Use.Alc")
  )

opt_age_race_data <- opt_data |> 
  dplyr::select(
    c("PID", "Group", 
      "Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education")
  )

opt_previous_preg_data <- opt_data |> 
  dplyr::select(
    c("PID", "Group", 
      "Prev.preg",
      "previous_live_preterm_birth",
      "Spont.ab", "Induced.ab", "Any.stillbirth")
  )

opt_clinical_data <- opt_data |> 
  dplyr::select(
    c("PID", "Group", 
      "Diabetes", "Hypertension", "Use.Alc")
  )
```


## Using `tbl_stack`

In the previous section, we have completed creating our three tables as shown below.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### 
Click on the different tabs to see the tables

#### Age, Race, Education

```{webr}
#| label: age race education summary table
#| envir: table_1
#| autorun: true
opt_age_race_table <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c("Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education"),
    by = "Group",
    label = list(
      "Age" ~ "Age - yr",
      "Hisp" ~ "Hispanic",
      "Education" ~ "Education - no. (%)"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{mean}±{sd}",
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p})"
    ),
    digits = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ 1,
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
    )
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_variable_group_header(
    header = "Race or ethnic group - no. (%)",
    variables = c("White", "Black", "Hisp")
  )|> 
  gtsummary::add_p(
    pvalue_fun = gtsummary::label_style_pvalue(digits = 2)
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header()

opt_age_race_table
```

#### Previous Pregnancy

```{webr}
#| caption: previous preg summary table
#| label: previous preg summary table
#| envir: table_1
#| autorun: true
opt_previous_preg_data <- opt_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c(
      "Prev.preg",
      "previous_live_preterm_birth",
      "Spont.ab", "Induced.ab", "Any.stillbirth"

    by = "Group",

      "Induced.ab" ~ "Induced abortion",
      "Any.stillbirth" ~ "Stillbirth"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p})"
    ),
    digits = list(
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
    )
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_variable_group_header(
    header = "Previous pregnancies - no. (%)",
    variables = c(
      "Prev.preg",
      "previous_live_preterm_birth",
      "Spont.ab", "Induced.ab", "Any.stillbirth"
    )
  )|> 
  gtsummary::add_p(
    pvalue_fun = gtsummary::label_style_pvalue(digits = 2)
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header()

opt_previous_preg_data
```

#### Clinical

```{webr}
#| caption: clinical summary table
#| label: clinical summary table
#| envir: table_1
#| autorun: true
p_value_style <- function(x) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    x == 1 ~ "1.0",
    x > 0.99 & x < 1 ~ "0.99",
    .default = gtsummary::style_pvalue(x, digits = 2)
  )
}
opt_clincal_data <- opt_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c("Diabetes", "Hypertension", "Use.Alc"),
    by = "Group",
    missing = "no",
    label = list(
      "Diabetes" ~ "Diabetes",
      "Hypertension" ~ "Chronic hypertension",
      "Use.Alc" ~ "Self-reported alcohol use"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{mean}±{sd}",
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p})"
    ),
    digits = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ 1,
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
    )
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_variable_group_header(
    header = "Coexisiting medical condition - no. (%)",
    variables = c("Diabetes", "Hypertension", "Use.Alc")
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_p(
    pvalue_fun = p_value_style
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header()

opt_clincal_data
```

:::

We use [gtsummary::tbl_stack](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_stack.html){target="_blank"} to append the three tables together.

```{webr}
#| caption: stack table1
#| label: stack table1
#| envir: table_1
table1 <- gtsummary::tbl_stack(
    tbls = list(opt_age_race_table, opt_previous_preg_data, opt_clincal_data)
  )

table1
```

## Understanding `gtsummary` object

We can now work on customising the table itself. To do this, we need to understand more about the [`gtsummary` object](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/articles/gtsummary_definition.html){target="_blank"}.

Every `gtsummary` object is a list comprising of, at minimum `table_body`, `table_styling`. Here is how you can extract `table_body` and `table_styling` and print the `header_names`.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### 
Click on the different tabs.

### table_body

`table_body` object is the data frame that defines what gets printed as the output. The compulsory columns are `variable`, `row_type` and `label`. `label` depicts what is printed at the `Characteristic` column. `stat_1` depicts what is printed at the `Control` column. `stat_2` depicts what is printed at `Treatment` column. `p.value` is printed at the `p-value` column.

```{webr}
#| caption: table1 table_body
#| label: table1 table_body
#| envir: table_1
table1 <- gtsummary::tbl_stack(
    tbls = list(opt_age_race_table, opt_previous_preg_data, opt_clincal_data)
  )

table1_body <- table1$table_body

table1_body |> 
  reactable::reactable(
    filterable = TRUE,
    paginationType = "jump",
    defaultPageSize = 5,
    minRows = 5)
```

### table_styling

`table_styling` objects is a list of data frames containing information about how `table_body` is printed, formatted and styled.

```{webr}
#| caption: table1 table_styling
#| label: table1 table_styling
#| envir: table_1
table1 <- gtsummary::tbl_stack(
    tbls = list(opt_age_race_table, opt_previous_preg_data, opt_clincal_data)
  )

table1_styling <- table1$table_styling

table1_styling |> 
  listviewer::reactjson()
```

### header_names

[`gtsummary::show_header_names()`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/modify.html){target="_blank"} prints the header/columns= names as text to the console.

```{webr}
#| caption: table1 header_names
#| label: table1 header_names
#| envir: table_1
table1 <- gtsummary::tbl_stack(
    tbls = list(opt_age_race_table, opt_previous_preg_data, opt_clincal_data)
  )

table1 |> 
  gtsummary::show_header_names()

```

:::

## Modify Header

After combining the tables, we first update the header using [`gtsummary::modify_header`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/modify.html){target="_blank"}.

As we use the `by` parameter in [`gtsummary::tbl_summary`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_summary.html){target="_blank"}, the following fields are available the stratifying columns: `{level}`, `{n}`, and `{p}`.

To match [Table 1](https://www.nejm.org/cms/10.1056/NEJMoa062249/asset/c676621f-111e-4299-a7a3-082bbe922f9a/assets/images/large/nejmoa062249_t1.jpg){target="_blank"}, we bold and add brackets to `N = 410` and `N = 413` in the column `stat_1` and `stat_2`. In addition, we update `p-value` to `P value` in the column `p.value`.


```{webr}
#| caption: modify header in table1
#| label: modify header in table1
#| envir: table_1
table1 <- gtsummary::tbl_stack(
    tbls = list(opt_age_race_table, opt_previous_preg_data, opt_clincal_data)
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::modify_header(
    stat_1 = "**Control Group**  \n**(N = {n})**",
    stat_2 = "**Treatment Group**  \n**(N = {n})**",
    p.value = "**P value**",
    text_interpret = "md"
  ) |>
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header()
  
table1
```


```{webr}
#| caption: table1 updated header_names
#| label: table1 updated header_names
#| envir: table_1
table1 |> 
  gtsummary::show_header_names()

```

## Next Steps

The next few steps is to add footnotes for the title as well as some rows in the tables. However, the way to do this varies based on what kind of output (html or word document) you wish the table to be represented as. `gtsummary` has its limitations in this and need the help of other R packages such as `gt` and `flextable`. Below are examples on how this can be done. 

### Export in html

We proceed to export the table as html by using the R package `gt`.

#### Add footnotes in table

Footnotes in the table can be added using [`gtsummary::modify_footnote_body`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/modify_footnote2.html){target="_blank"}.

To match [Table 1](https://www.nejm.org/cms/10.1056/NEJMoa062249/asset/c676621f-111e-4299-a7a3-082bbe922f9a/assets/images/large/nejmoa062249_t1.jpg){target="_blank"}, we add the relevant footnotes at the relevant rows in the `table_body` data frame.

```{webr}
#| caption: add table footnotes table1
#| label: add table footnotes table1 by modify_footnote_body
#| envir: table_1
table1_html <- gtsummary::tbl_stack(
    tbls = list(opt_age_race_table, opt_previous_preg_data, opt_clincal_data)
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::modify_header(
    stat_1 = "**Control Group**  \n**(N = {n})**",
    stat_2 = "**Treatment Group**  \n**(N = {n})**",
    p.value = "**P value**",
    text_interpret = "md"
  ) |>
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header() |> 
  gtsummary::modify_footnote_body(
    footnote = "Race or ethnic group was reported by the patients. Some women selected more than one category and were included in all.",
    columns = "label",
    rows = .data[["label"]] == "Race or ethnic group - no. (%)" & 
           .data[["row_type"]] == "variable_group"
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::modify_footnote_body(
    footnote = "Some patients reported more than one event.",
    columns = "label",
    rows = .data[["label"]] %in% c("Previous pregnancies - no. (%)")  & 
           .data[["row_type"]] == "variable_group"
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::modify_footnote_body(
    footnote = "Percentages are based on 263 women in the control group and 261 women in the treatment group who had had any live births.",
    columns = "label",
    rows = .data[["var_label"]] %in% c("Live preterm birth") & 
           .data[["row_type"]] == "label"
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::modify_footnote_body(
    footnote = "Percentages are based on 305 women in the control group and 306 women in the treatment group who had had any previous pregnacies.",
    columns = "label",
    rows = .data[["var_label"]] %in% c("Spontaneous abortion", "Induced abortion", "Stillbirth")  & 
           .data[["row_type"]] == "label"
  )

table1_html
```

#### Add Title with footnotes

`gtsummary` does not have a function to add footnote at headers. You must proceed to convert the `gtsummary` object to `gt` and continue the work from there.

```{webr}
#| caption: complete table1 html
#| label: complete table1 html
#| envir: table_1
table1_html <- table1_html |> 
  gtsummary::as_gt() |> 
  gt::tab_header(
    title = "Table 1. Baseline Characteristics of the Study Patients"
  ) |> 
  gt::tab_options(heading.align = "left") |> 
  gt::tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Plus-minus values are means±SD.",
    locations = gt::cells_title(groups = "title")
  ) |> 
  gt::opt_footnote_marks(marks = c("*", "†", "‡", "§", "¶")) |> 
  gt::opt_footnote_spec(
    spec_ref = "i",   # Removes '^' (superscript), keeps italics 'i'
    spec_ftr = "x"    # Unstyled or baseline text for the footer
  )

table1_html
```

#### Save as html

```{webr}
#| caption: download table1 html
#| label: download table1 html
#| envir: table_1
# Use https://georgestagg.github.io/pandoc-wasm/ to convert
table1_html |> 
  gt::gtsave(filename = "data/table1.html")

downloadthis::download_file(
  path = "data/table1.html"
)

```

### Export in word

We proceed to export the table as html by using the R package `flextable`.

#### Add footnotes in table

Footnotes in the table are this time added using [`gtsummary::modify_table_body`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/modify_table_body.html){target="_blank"} as though we can add footnote in `flextable`, they are always represented as superscript.

```{webr}
#| caption: add table footnotes table1
#| label: add table footnotes table1 by modify_table_body
#| envir: table_1
table1_word <- gtsummary::tbl_stack(
    tbls = list(opt_age_race_table, opt_previous_preg_data, opt_clincal_data)
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::modify_header(
    stat_1 = "**Control Group**  \n**(N = {n})**",
    stat_2 = "**Treatment Group**  \n**(N = {n})**",
    p.value = "**P value**",
    text_interpret = "md"
  ) |>
  gtsummary::modify_table_body(
    ~ .x |> 
      dplyr::mutate(
        `label` = dplyr::case_when(
          .data[["label"]] == "Race or ethnic group - no. (%)" ~ "Race or ethnic group - no. (%)†",
          .data[["label"]] == "Previous pregnancies - no. (%)" ~ "Previous pregnancies - no. (%)‡",
          .data[["label"]] == "Live preterm birth" ~ "Live preterm birth§",
          .data[["label"]] %in% c(
            "Spontaneous abortion", "Induced abortion", "Stillbirth"
          ) ~ paste0(.data[["label"]], "¶"),
          .default = .data[["label"]]
        )
      )
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header()

table1_word
```

#### Add Title with footnotes

We proceed to convert the `gtsummary` object to `flextable` and continue the work from there.

```{webr}
#| caption: complete table1 word
#| label: complete table1 word
#| envir: table_1
table1_word <- table1_word |> 
  gtsummary::as_flex_table() |> 
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = flextable::as_paragraph(
      flextable::as_b("Table 1. Baseline Characteristics of the Study Patients"),
      flextable::as_chunk("*", props = flextable::fp_text_default(vertical.align = "baseline"))
    ), 
    align_with_table = FALSE,
    fp_p = officer::fp_par(padding = 0),
  ) |> 
  flextable::add_footer_lines(values = "* Plus-minus values are means±SD.") |> 
  flextable::add_footer_lines(values = "† Race or ethnic group was reported by the patients. Some women selected more than one category and were included in all.") |>
  flextable::add_footer_lines(values = "‡ Some patients reported more than one event.") |>
  flextable::add_footer_lines(values = "§ Percentages are based on 263 women in the control group and 261 women in the treatment group who had had any live births.") |>
  flextable::add_footer_lines(values = "¶ Percentages are based on 305 women in the control group and 306 women in the treatment group who had had any previous pregnacies.")

table1_word

```

#### Save as word

```{webr}
#| caption: download table1 word
#| label: download table1 word
#| envir: table_1
table1_word |> 
  flextable::save_as_docx( path = "data/table1.docx")

downloadthis::download_file(
  path = "data/table1.docx"
)

```
